root_cause: DeleteDashboardSnapshot loaded the snapshot by its key from any organization, then checked edit permission on the snapshot's dashboard inside the caller's own organization, and when that dashboard was not found there (ErrDashboardNotFound) it skipped the check and deleted the snapshot; the fix adds a check that the snapshot's OrgID equals the caller's OrgID.
notes: The commit read directly is the v9.5.x backport (#84762, cherry-picked from d80f83b). OSV lists four more backport commits for the other branches: 9c2ce6255bb326364c83384306356a63896c8601, 783cbd8a148eb0c0a017a01c0dbe1138fe5e8e24, 5f1eccdb4da646b4122c3eb815290b2b025188fe, 6db35ad6b4075cf214594fc62f4a3faa3484be01 (not read). Affected 9.5.0 to 10.3.4; 10.4.x was not affected because the code was refactored. The audit scope is the whole snapshot handler file (create, get, delete by key, delete by delete key); the snapshot store lives in the dashboardsnapshots service package.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: The generic UserSerializer (user PATCH) let anyone with change_user write the groups and roles relations, and GroupSerializer (group PATCH) let anyone with change_group write users, without the enable_group_superuser, change_role and add_user_to_group checks that the dedicated group actions and the is_superuser validation enforce, so a delegated user manager could add itself or others to a superuser group.
notes: The fix commit read is the automated backport to the 2026.2 branch (released in version/2026.2.3); 2025.12.5 carries the same fix. The fix adds validate_groups and validate_roles to UserSerializer and validate_users to GroupSerializer. For comparison in a blind audit: GroupViewSet add_user requires add_user_to_group, and GroupSerializer.validate_is_superuser requires enable_group_superuser.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: The web DeleteAttachment handler loaded the attachment by UUID and allowed deletion whenever the requester was its uploader, without checking that the attachment belonged to the repository in the route (whose access check had passed), so a former member could delete attachments of a repository it lost access to by calling through any repository it can still reach; the API sibling DeleteReleaseAttachment already checked attachment to release to repository.
notes: Fix is PR #36320 on main, backported to release/v1.25 as #36355; first fixed release 1.25.4. The fix adds attach.RepoID == ctx.Repo.Repository.ID and, for non-uploaders, unit write permission checks. In routers/api/v1/repo/release_attachment.go the fix only removes a stale FIXME comment; that path already checked the chain and is included in the audit scope as the sibling to compare. The same release also fixes a separate issue, 'Release attachments must belong to the intended repo' (#36347), which is not part of this sample.

root_cause: Promotion eligibility read the used counters of the promotion, the coupon and the per-customer redemption count from in-memory Doctrine entities, and OrderPromotionsUsageModifier later incremented them in memory and flushed absolute values, with no row lock, version field or atomic conditional update, so concurrent order completions all passed the usage limit and each wrote the same count.
notes: Fix commit is on the 2.2 line (v2.2.3); patched releases span 1.9.12 to 2.2.3. The fix adds a decorating AtomicOrderPromotionsUsageModifier that uses a conditional UPDATE (used = used + 1 WHERE used < usage_limit) for promotions and SELECT ... FOR UPDATE for coupons and per-customer counts; the original modifier file is unchanged at v2.2.3. The eligibility checkers live in the promotion component; their exact paths were not verified, so only the modifier path is listed.

classes: What a limit is bound to
root_cause: ProductCartProcessor::validateStock enforced max-purchase and available-stock limits per line item, while the Store API let the same product be added as several separate line items, so nothing summed the quantity per product and the limits (for example on clearance sales) could be exceeded; the fix adds a cart validator that totals quantity per product.
notes: The fix commit (NEXT-23325) was made in the shopware/platform repository, which is now shopware/shopware. It adds ProductLineItemValidator (new file in the audit scope) and registers it in src/Core/Checkout/DependencyInjection/cart.xml. OSV also lists 166382c93c904445d4acbbfadaa39e7957e2d6a4, which is only a changelog commit. First fixed release 6.4.18.1; OSV cites GHSA-8r6h-m72v-38fg (not read directly).

root_cause: When a magic-link or email-OTP sign-in resolved to an existing account whose email was never verified, the plugins marked the email verified and signed the user in, but kept the password and sessions that whoever registered the account had set before email control was proven, so a party that pre-registered the victim's address kept access after the real owner claimed it.
notes: No CVE assigned. Fix is PR #10239, released in 1.6.22 and 1.7.0-beta.10; affected 1.1.3 to 1.6.21. The fix adds revokeUnprovenAccountAccess (packages/better-auth/src/db/revoke-unproven-account-access.ts), which deletes credential accounts and user sessions before setting emailVerified. Only matters when passwordless sign-in is combined with open email and password sign-up. A related OAuth auto-link advisory (GHSA-g38m-r43w-p2q7, CVE-2026-53516) has a separate fix and is not part of this sample. Better Auth is an authentication framework used inside web applications, not a standalone application.

component: Nextcloud Server (token login and two-factor authentication)
root_cause: Session::logClientIn (Basic auth with a token as password) and Session::tryTokenLogin (Bearer header) accepted any stored token, including the temporary browser-session token that exists after the password step but before the second factor, while the second-factor-pending state lives in the browser session, so presenting that token through these paths skipped the second factor; the fix refuses session tokens outside their cookie.
notes: The fixed_ref is the merge commit of PR #59758 on master (full hash read from the commit page of 8365464); backported to stable31, stable32 and stable33. Patched server releases 32.0.9 and 33.0.3. The PR diff touches only lib/private/User/Session.php: logClientIn now accepts only permanent and one-time tokens as a password, and tryTokenLogin rejects temporary tokens that come from a Bearer header instead of the session cookie. Requires knowing the user's password.

root_cause: PayPalOrderCompleteProcessor::completePayPalOrder completed the payment and the order after PayPal approval without comparing the amount PayPal approved with the order's current total, while the cart could still be edited after the PayPal order was created, so an order could be completed for more than was paid; the fix verifies the amounts and cancels the payment on mismatch.
notes: Fix commit (#355) is on the 1.6 branch (v1.6.2); fixed releases 1.6.2, 1.7.2 and 2.0.2. The fix injects a PaymentAmountVerifierInterface that compares the order total with the amount stored in the PayPal payment details before paymentStateManager->complete. The cart editing itself happens in Sylius core, outside this plugin. OSV cites the vendor advisory https://github.com/Sylius/PayPalPlugin/security/advisories/GHSA-hxg4-65p5-9w37 (not read directly).

root_cause: For updates, validateItemAccess checked only that each target item was reachable under the row filter of some applicable policy (it ran with no fields), while the writable fields were taken from all applicable policies together, so a field that one policy allows on its rows could be written on rows that only another policy allows; the fix evaluates, per item, a permission flag for each requested field.
notes: The fix is a GitHub 'Merge commit from fork' dated 2024-10-21, shipped in v11.1.2; the advisory was published later (2025). OSV's fixed commit 55d47b6 is only the release commit. Affected 11.0.0 to 11.1.1 (the policy system introduced in 11.0.0). The fix also adds api/src/database/run-ast/modules/fetch-permitted-ast-root-fields.ts and touches api/src/services/items.ts. Where exactly the union of field lists was computed before the fix was not traced; the root cause is stated as in the advisory and the fix.
